# AI Engineering Harness

> An engineering organisation of 18 AI agents wired into one closed loop. It does
> not make AI agents write code faster; it makes their output checkable. Code
> reaches `main` only when CI is green, at least two cold-start reviewers approve,
> and the evidence pack is complete.

Installed as a skill into 40 CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
Gemini, Qwen and others). MIT licensed. Current version 0.2.2.

## What it is

A harness, not a model. It supplies the roles, workflows, templates and gates that
turn fast AI-generated code into reviewable engineering work: issue intake,
worktree isolation, planning, implementation, adversarial review, an evidence
pack, merge, and a memory write-back so the next session starts from a conclusion
rather than re-deriving it.

## Install

```
npx -y skills add lora-sys/ai-engineering-harness -g --all --full-depth
```

Then, in the repository being taken over: "Use $ai-engineering-harness to take
over this repo." It runs a scan first and names what it found — category and worst
location — before asking anything.

## Skill family

- `ai-engineering-harness`: the closed loop itself — agents, workflows, gates
- `build-agent-app`: scaffolding for agent applications
- `frontend-creative`: Awwwards-grade creative web UI, not dashboards
- `dashboard`: optional observation panel — Quick Scan and a local board

## Quick Scan

Ten heuristics for inherited "vibe-coded" repositories: hardcoded secrets, missing
error handling, duplicated logic, style drift, missing test coverage, intent loss
(code contradicting its own doc comment), commented-out code, orphan TODOs, dead
code after early return, and absent tests. It reports a chaos score plus the
specific categories and worst locations, and can group findings into tracked
issues.
